description: We are a group of students from SMU Computer Science. We enjoy solving problems and turning them into practical solutions.
summary:
FireSafe-SI is an SI-powered dashboard that turns decades of NASA microgravity combustion research into fire-safety insight for crews heading to the Moon and Mars. It connects live to NASA's Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) repository, pulling 24 combustion investigations (BASS, Saffire, FLEX, ACME and more), 352 publications and about 2,000 experimental test records, then normalizes messy test tables into comparable oxygen, pressure, flow and fuel conditions.

The SI layer summarizes each investigation in a plain-language brief, ranks every experiment by relevance to a chosen habitat (ISS, Orion, Moon Base, pressurized rover, Mars, spacesuit) with transparent, explainable scores, and answers questions in a streaming chat that cites the source records. Engineers can compare studies side by side, plot raw data and export it for model calibration.

Most importantly, it shows what is missing. Our gap analysis found that no solid-material flammability test in PSI exceeds about 22% O2, and no tested condition falls inside the planned Moon Base atmosphere (≥30% O2, ≤10.2 psi), where materials burn far more readily. FireSafe-SI tells mission planners which data they can trust today and which experiments must come next.
details: FireSafe-SI turns NASA's scattered microgravity combustion data into answers for crew fire safety. An ingestion service connects live to the public JSON API of NASA's Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) repository. We found this API by inspecting PSI's web front end. The service pulls 24 combustion investigations (BASS, BASS-II, Saffire I–III, FLEX, FLEX-2, ACME, SPICE, SLICE, DAFT and others), their 352 publications, and 22 experimental test-matrix CSVs with about 2,000 test records. The test tables are messy: "0.17; 0.21;0.25; 0.3", "757.7 mmHg", "~ 21.5", "LOW O2". A profiler normalizes them into comparable oxygen (%), pressure (atm/psi), flow (cm/s), fuel and sample-geometry values, and it records which parameters were varied and which were held constant.
